title: The Wrong Winter
premise: Folklorist Theo Yarrow has spent three years in the village of Hollowmere, recording songs the residents refuse to sing twice and telling himself the winter noises have rational explanations. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside, the count begins again — a tally of names that must be filled before spring, and Theo's family is on it. To save them, he must convince the last holdout resident to sign away her claim to belonging, breaking the village's covenant, even as he falls in love with her granddaughter. In the end, Theo signs his own name in place of theirs, learning that survival's price is always paid by someone who chooses to stay.
about_author: Cyrus Eastwick is the pen name of a former archivist of regional folk music collections, whose fieldwork in remote northern villages left him with more unanswered questions than recordings. He writes horror from a farmhouse that is, he insists, perfectly ordinary after dark.

chapters.title: Songs They Won't Sing Twice
chapters.summary: Theo Yarrow records an elderly singer who stops mid-verse, pale, refusing to continue. His sister Mara and nephew Ivo have joined him for the winter, and Theo notices the villagers watching them with something like pity. POV: Theo. Beat: unease disguised as academic curiosity; the reader senses the family has walked into something.

chapters.title: The Excavation
chapters.summary: A crew digging foundations for new cottages strikes stone beneath the frost line. Theo arrives to find a door of black oak set into the earth, its iron hinges fused, sealed from the inside. The foreman jokes about it; the villagers do not. POV: Theo. Beat: dread crystallizes from folklore into physical fact.

chapters.title: What the Door Was For
chapters.summary: Theo interviews Wren Halloway, the last resident who hasn't signed the parish papers ceding common land. Her grandmother's journal describes 'the counting winters' — seasons when the village owed names. Wren warns him to leave before the thaw. POV: Theo. Beat: first real knowledge, first real warning ignored.

chapters.title: Noises With Explanations
chapters.summary: Scratching beneath the floorboards. Ivo swears someone sang his name outside his window. Theo catalogs each sound with a rational cause — pipes, wind, foxes — but his list grows shorter than his fears. POV: Theo, with a brief Mara interlude. Beat: the rationalist's scaffolding begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Papers
chapters.summary: The parish council pressures Wren to sign; hers is the final signature needed to legally dissolve the old covenant. She refuses, telling Theo that signatures are how the village 'pays' — and that this year the payment is overdue. POV: alternating Theo and Wren. Beat: duty versus self-preservation made explicit.

chapters.title: Ivo Counts
chapters.summary: Eight-year-old Ivo begins compulsively counting aloud at dusk — thirteen, fourteen, fifteen — numbers no one taught him. Mara finds tally marks scratched inside his closet, from the inside. POV: Mara. Beat: maternal terror; the horror now has a child's face.

chapters.title: The First Name
chapters.summary: Old Tam Ellery, the foreman who joked about the door, is found frozen solid in a warm room, his mouth full of soil. On the door below ground, a fresh notch appears in the wood. The count has started taking. POV: Theo. Beat: denial dies; the stakes become mortal.

chapters.title: Wren's Grandmother
chapters.summary: Wren gives Theo the journal. It reveals the covenant: every generation, the village signs away its dead or its newcomers, and one family always stays behind to keep the count honest. Wren's line has kept it for two hundred years. POV: Theo. Beat: the rules are clear now — and cruel.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Theo and Wren grow close over late nights translating the journal, an intimacy both know the covenant forbids: she belongs to the village, he belongs to the count. A kiss in the snow that neither apologizes for. POV: alternating. Beat: tenderness blooming in hostile ground.

chapters.title: The Village Sings
chapters.summary: At midnight the whole village stands in the square singing the forbidden song — once, together, complete. Theo realizes they aren't summoning anything; they're holding it back, and they've been doing it for centuries. POV: Theo. Beat: awe and horror fused; the enemy may be the only protection.

chapters.title: Mara Tries to Leave
chapters.summary: Mara packs the car at dawn. Every road out of Hollowmere loops back to the square. The fuel gauge reads full, then empty, then full. Something in the back seat breathes. POV: Mara. Beat: claustrophobic despair; there is no exit, only terms.

chapters.title: The Second Name
chapters.summary: The schoolteacher vanishes; her classroom chalkboard is covered in tally marks reaching thirty-one. The council tells Theo quietly: the count wants three more before thaw, and it prefers names that don't belong. POV: Theo. Beat: the pattern points at his family.

chapters.title: What Signing Means
chapters.summary: Theo deciphers the final pages: whoever signs the papers in the last resident's stead takes the keeping — becomes the one who stays, forever, beneath the door. Wren begs him not to consider it. He already is. POV: Theo. Beat: love against duty turns inward; the sacrifice takes shape.

chapters.title: The Council's Bargain
chapters.summary: The council offers Theo a deal: sign, and Mara and Ivo walk free at thaw. But Wren reveals the fine print — the keeper's family is spared once, then forgotten by everyone who ever loved them. POV: Theo and Wren. Beat: the price of survival revealed as erasure, not death.

chapters.title: Ivo Is Taken
chapters.summary: One night the house goes silent. Ivo's bed is cold, the window open onto unbroken snow, small footprints leading toward the excavation site and stopping at nothing. The door below ground has a new notch, small and shallow. POV: Mara. Beat: the darkest hour; grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Below
chapters.summary: Theo breaks the seal's outer ward and descends through the door — into a corridor of doors, each carved with a name and a year, stretching back centuries. He hears Ivo counting somewhere in the dark, and something counting back. POV: Theo. Beat: descent into the heart of the mystery; courage born of guilt.

chapters.title: The Keeper
chapters.summary: Theo finds the previous keeper — Wren's grandmother, unchanged since 1961 — tending Ivo in a room of warm soil. She explains: the count isn't hunger, it's bookkeeping. Someone must always be owed, and someone must always pay. POV: Theo. Beat: the antagonist reframed as a tragic office.

chapters.title: Wren Signs
chapters.summary: Above, Wren makes her choice: she signs the papers herself, claiming the keeping before Theo can, trading her belonging for his family's freedom. The village feels it instantly — every door in Hollowmere unlocks. POV: Wren. Beat: love against duty resolved by reversal; she pays so he won't have to.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Theo refuses to leave without her. In the corridor of doors he offers the count a substitution it has never been offered: his name freely given, beside hers, two keepers where one was owed. The old ledger accepts what no one has dared write. POV: Theo. Beat: climax — defiance of the rules by exceeding them.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Spring comes early. Mara and Ivo wake in their own beds with no memory of Hollowmere at all. The village sings the song twice, joyfully, for the first time in living memory. The excavation site is empty earth, the door gone as if never dug up. POV: Mara. Beat: bittersweet release; salvation purchased with forgetting.

chapters.title: The Songs Remain
chapters.summary: Mara, back in the city, finds a tape in Theo's recorder: his voice and Wren's, singing the forbidden song all the way through, twice, laughing between verses. She plays it for Ivo, who hums along to words he was never taught. POV: Mara. Beat: grief and grace intertwined; love outlasting erasure.

chapters.title: The Wrong Winter
chapters.summary: Years later, a new folklorist arrives in Hollowmere asking about songs no one will sing twice. An old woman with familiar eyes serves her tea and says the winter was wrong this year — too long, too hungry. Beneath the floorboards, faintly, two voices keep the count together. POV: the newcomer, briefly, then Wren. Beat: cyclical resolution — the price endures, but no one pays it alone.
